Lindquist RA.lab_name: Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research (Cambridge, Massachusetts, USA)
Lindquist RA.role: Co-author of the Atlas studies SAN2008 (Rag GTPases and amino acid signaling) and SAN2007 (PRAS40 as an insulin-regulated brake on mTORC1).
Lindquist RA.sub: Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research, Cambridge, MA, USA
story: Robert A Lindquist is a middle author on two cell-biology papers in the Atlas. The 2007 paper identified PRAS40 as an insulin-controlled brake inside mTORC1: without insulin PRAS40 holds the complex shut, and insulin makes Akt phosphorylate PRAS40 so the brake lets go. The 2008 paper found that the Rag GTPases bind raptor and let mTORC1 sense amino acids, by controlling whether mTOR sits near its activator Rheb.

PubMed does not list an affiliation for him in these two records. The link to the Whitehead Institute comes from a related paper from the same group (a Drosophila RNAi screen of TORC1 signaling), where PubMed lists him there and where several co-authors of the Atlas papers also appear.

highlights.SAN2008: Middle author of the paper on Rag GTPases and amino acid signaling to mTORC1.
highlights.SAN2007: Middle author of the paper on PRAS40 as an insulin-regulated inhibitor of mTORC1.

Medina DL.lab_name: Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine (TIGEM) (Pozzuoli, Naples, Italy)
Medina DL.role: Co-author of the Atlas study SET2012 (lysosome-to-nucleus signaling through mTOR and TFEB).
Medina DL.sub: Telethon Institute of Genetics and Medicine (TIGEM), Pozzuoli, Naples, Italy
story: Diego L Medina is a middle author of a 2012 paper that studied how the lysosome, the cell's recycling compartment, tells the nucleus what it needs. In cells, mTORC1 on the lysosome surface adds a phosphate to the transcription factor TFEB and keeps it inactive. When mTORC1 is blocked, or when the cell is starved or the lysosome is stressed, TFEB moves into the nucleus and turns on lysosome and autophagy genes.

PubMed gives no affiliation for him in this record. The Telethon Institute (TIGEM) comes from two related papers from the same group, where PubMed lists him there and where co-authors of this study also appear.

highlights.SET2012: Middle author of the paper on the lysosome-to-nucleus mTOR and TFEB mechanism.

Carling D.lab_name: Cellular Stress Group, MRC Clinical Sciences Centre, Imperial College (London, United Kingdom)
Carling D.role: Co-author of the Atlas study XIA2011 (structure of mammalian AMPK and its regulation by ADP).
Carling D.sub: Cellular Stress Group, MRC Clinical Sciences Centre, Imperial College, London, UK
story: David Carling is a middle author of a 2011 structural paper on AMPK, the cell's energy sensor that works against mTORC1 when energy is low. The study showed that AMP binding protects AMPK from losing its activating phosphate, that ADP binding at one site gives the same protection without switching the enzyme on, and it reported the crystal structure of an active AMPK complex.

PubMed gives no affiliation for him in this record. The Cellular Stress Group at the MRC Clinical Sciences Centre comes from a 2013 paper by the same team, where PubMed lists him there next to many co-authors of the 2011 study. He is also listed in a second Atlas paper (SEL2009, S6K1 and lifespan in mice), but that study is not covered here because the available records did not confirm the same affiliation.

highlights.XIA2011: Middle author of the paper on the structure of mammalian AMPK and its regulation by ADP.

Gamblin SJ.lab_name: MRC National Institute for Medical Research (London, United Kingdom)
Gamblin SJ.role: Senior (last) author of the Atlas study XIA2011 (structure of mammalian AMPK and its regulation by ADP).
Gamblin SJ.sub: MRC National Institute for Medical Research, Mill Hill, London, UK
story: Steven J Gamblin is the last author of a 2011 paper on the structure of AMPK, the cell's energy sensor that works against mTORC1 when energy is low. The work found that AMP binding protects AMPK from losing its activating phosphate, that ADP binding at one site gives the same protection without activating the enzyme, and it solved the crystal structure of an active AMPK complex.

PubMed gives an affiliation only for the first author in this record. The Mill Hill institute for Gamblin comes from a 2013 paper by the same team, where PubMed lists him at the MRC National Institute for Medical Research in London.

highlights.XIA2011: Last author of the paper on the structure of mammalian AMPK and its regulation by ADP.
